goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sector GDP contracted 1.3% month-over-month while holding +3.5% year-over-year1. Lead export commodities remained elevated: wheat priced $655, up 22.9% Y/Y and 7.8% W/W, while Western SPF lumber held $584.50/mfbm, up 5.2% Y/Y2. Potash (Nutrien proxy) sat at $97.34, up 22.2% Y/Y but down 4.1% M/M2.

The project database tracks 14 discrete projects ($4.74B) — roughly 2 agriculture and 12 forestry — a research-led rather than project-led pipeline3. The 12 forestry projects ($4.73B) sit against U.S. Section 232 plus AD/CVD measures that raise Canadian producer costs an estimated 25-30%; Western Forest Products extended its Chemainus, B.C. sawmill closure through end of 20264.

Sector capital flows largely through policy channels. Farm Credit Canada convened a coalition of 20+ investment organizations prepared to deploy up to $5 billion by 2030, totalling $7 billion with FCC's May 2025 commitment5. The five-year $3.5-billion Sustainable Canadian Agricultural Partnership continues, with $75 million added over five years to AgriMarketing market-diversification streams6. If U.S. trade measures persist, additional sawmill closures and rural employment contraction would extend the forestry sub-sector divergence from the +3.5% Y/Y aggregate.

goodsIndustries.name: Mining, Quarrying & Oil/Gas Extraction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Mining, quarrying and oil/gas extraction sector GDP rose 0.4% month-over-month and 3.6% year-over-year1. WTI crude averaged $100.16/bbl, up 5% W/W and 62.5% Y/Y; copper held $6.34/lb, up 36.5% Y/Y; iron ore sat at $16.58, up 69.4% Y/Y; gold reached $4,563, up 41.7% Y/Y but down 3.3% W/W2.

The database tracks 442 mining and oil/gas projects ($324.69B) — 347 mining ($227.11B) and 39 oil/gas ($97.58B) — with 43 new mining projects added in the last 21 days3. The cross-reference engine links 26 Alberta oil/gas projects ($44.43B) to WTI at $100.16/bbl, above the breakeven range cited for oil-sands proposals; 2026 oil-and-gas capex is estimated near $50B3. Western Canada drilling averaged 213 active rigs in 2026, with oil-sands proposals totalling 4.1 million bbl/d combined capacity4.

Federal policy unlocked additional capital. Canada secured 30 new critical-minerals partnerships tied to $12.1 billion in mining-project capital, plus $165.2M for 22 projects unlocking $434M across eight provinces and a $1.5 billion First and Last Mile Fund for mine-supporting infrastructure5. Junior exploration 2026 intentions point to a record $2.91 billion4. If commodity prices hold, the 442-project pipeline would operate under supportive margin conditions.

goodsIndustries.name: Utilities (Electricity, Gas, Water)
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Utilities sector GDP was flat month-over-month and down 4.0% year-over-year, the steepest annual decline among goods industries1. Natural gas priced $2.92, up 5.9% W/W but down 13.2% Y/Y2. The TSX infrastructure basket sat at 55.94, up 28.5% Y/Y2. Canada produced 623 TWh of electricity in 2024, 65% renewable and 78% non-GHG (hydro 57.4%, nuclear 13.5%)3.

The database tracks 1,441 utilities, power and water projects ($489.23B), with 126 added in the last 21 days4. The GDP contraction coincides with forward-looking capital commitments and infrastructure valuations up 28.5% Y/Y. AI data-centre load is a new structural electricity-demand driver: Synapse Data Centre Inc. proposed a $10-billion data-centre-plus-gas-power plan in rural Alberta, and a Telus cluster scales from 85 to 150 MW5.

Natural Resources Canada is developing a Nuclear Energy Strategy for release at end of 2026, covering new builds, export, uranium and fuel expansion, and fusion innovation, alongside a $40-million 2026-27 microreactor assessment for remote DND facilities6. OPG and Port Hope reached an agreement for new nuclear at the Wesleyville site, with a project description submitted to IAAC and up to 10 GWe envisaged5. If the strategy and the BC 2025 call for power proceed as announced, additional generation capital would enter the pipeline.

goodsIndustries.name: Construction
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Construction sector GDP contracted 0.5% month-over-month while holding +2.8% year-over-year1. Key inputs rose: Western SPF lumber priced $584.50/mfbm, up 5.2% Y/Y and 1.4% W/W, while iron ore sat at $16.58, up 69.4% Y/Y and 2.4% W/W2. February 2026 construction GDP rose +0.2% with manufacturing-led activity, and heavy-civil labour demand concentrated in transit and energy corridors3.

The database tracks 1,075 infrastructure projects ($209.84B), with 44 added in the last 21 days; 419 are Under Construction and 118 Approved4. The 419 Under Construction projects face iron-ore inputs up 69.4% Y/Y and lumber up 5.2% Y/Y. Active heavy-civil work includes the George Massey Tunnel replacement ($4.15B, 8-lane, BC), the GO Transit Bowmanville Extension (18.7 km, broke ground January 2026), and the Queensborough Bridge upgrade ($20.8M contract, spring 2026 start)5.

Ontario's $210 billion-plus 10-year capital plan — including $37 billion in 2026-27 — represents the largest provincial capital plan in Canadian history, concentrated in urban transit, energy infrastructure, transportation corridors, port expansions, and regional utilities6. If the $37B 2026-27 tranche is released as scheduled, heavy-civil and transit-corridor activity would expand; if input-cost increases persist, project budgets in the 419 Under Construction set would face cost pressure.

goodsIndustries.name: Manufacturing
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Manufacturing sector GDP rose 1.8% month-over-month — the largest sector gain since January 2023 — while remaining -3.1% year-over-year1. The S&P Global Canada Manufacturing PMI rose to 53.3 in April 2026 from 50.0 in March, the strongest reading since June 20222. February manufacturing sales reached $71.2 billion, up 3.6% M/M, with durable goods up 3.6% leading the February GDP gain2. Copper, a key input, held $6.34/lb, up 36.5% Y/Y3.

The database tracks 73 manufacturing projects ($68.8B), excluding the suspended Honda Ontario $15B EV plant, which is recorded as Cancelled across four duplicate records and excluded to avoid a nominal $60B double-count4. Copper inputs up 36.5% Y/Y intersect EV and battery supply-chain projects; April PMI data noted input costs rising at the fastest pace in more than 3.5 years2.

Electra Battery Materials received a $20 million federal Strategic Response Fund investment toward a $99.4 million cobalt-sulfate refinery expansion in Temiskaming Shores, Ontario, part of the Critical Minerals Strategy battery build-out; Northvolt QC funding ended in September 20255. February's month-over-month momentum reverses the negative Y/Y trend, with January 2026 production at -4.20% Y/Y. If the PMI expansion holds, the Y/Y comparison would narrow through Q2 2026; if U.S. tariff uncertainty intensifies, the EV/battery project set would face delivery risk, as the Honda suspension already illustrates.
